title: The Badawi and His Wife (Español)

full_text:
The Caliph Harun al-Rashid, while traveling disguised as an ordinary traveler through the desert outside Kufa, became separated from his escort during a sudden sandstorm. Thirsty, exhausted, and covered in dust, he reached the solitary goat-hair tent of an impoverished Bedouin named Abu Mansur.

Abu Mansur welcomed the unknown wanderer with boundless warmth, washed his feet with cool well-water, and wrapped him in his only clean cloak.

Abu Mansur went to his wife behind the tent partition and whispered: 'We have an honored guest, but we possess only one small ewe whose milk feeds our infant son; what shall we do?'

His noble wife replied without hesitation: 'Shall a stranger sleep hungry under our tent? Slaughter the ewe, roast the meat with desert herbs, and bake our last cup of barley flour into flatbread! The Creator who brought the guest will provide for our child tomorrow.'

Abu Mansur slaughtered the ewe, and served a hot, savory feast before the Caliph, sitting beside him to ensure his comfort while keeping nothing for himself.

The next morning, Harun al-Rashid’s royal guards galloped up, flags flying, dismounting to prostrate themselves before the Caliph!

Abu Mansur and his wife turned pale with awe, realizing that they had entertained the Emperor of Baghdad!

Harun al-Rashid embraced the humble couple with tears in his eyes: 'You slaughtered your only ewe to feed an unknown traveler in the midnight storm! Today, the Emperor of the Faithful repays your bread.'

The Caliph gifted Abu Mansur a fertile oasis with a hundred date palms, a flock of five hundred sheep, and a thousand gold dinars, proving that an open hand in poverty earns the highest riches of heaven and earth.
moral: Hospitality that shares its last sustenance with the traveler earns royal favor and enduring blessings. [ES]
